q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT DISTINCT P1.EMAIL FROM PERSON P1, PERSON P2 WHERE P1.EMAIL = P2.EMAIL AND P1.ID != P2.ID

counterexample: INSERT INTO PERSON (ID, EMAIL) VALUES (1, 'example@example.com'); INSERT INTO PERSON (ID, EMAIL) VALUES (2, 'example@example.com');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 groups the person table by email and selects emails that have a count greater than 1, which means it finds emails that are associated with more than one person. Q2, on the other hand, finds distinct pairs of people who share the same email address, which means it identifies emails that are used by at least two different people.
counterexample_dsp: A test database with at least two people sharing the same email address.
